root_cause_criterion.criterion: Immediately after `len = snprintf(tmp, sizeof(tmp) - 1, "\\u%04x", codepoint);`, `flb_utils_write_str()` must reject any case where the computed unicode escape length `len` exceeds the remaining output budget `available - written` before it reaches a later escape sink.
root_cause_criterion.description: The crashing key reaches the line-710 unicode-escape path with only `available - written` bytes left in the current JSON buffer. The vulnerable code checks only for a 6-byte minimum before formatting the escape, but the actual formatted length can be larger. The fixed program enforces the missing post-`snprintf` conjunct on the sink-linked call, so the serializer either retries with a larger buffer or executes the later control-byte escape only after the unicode escape fits.
root_cause_criterion.verification_note: The required assertion is evaluated at the sink-linked unicode-escape root and is expected to be violated on the vulnerable original while the fixed original either satisfies it on a later retry or, if guarded, requires a boundary perturbation witness.

nodes.state: The sink-linked `encoded_to_buf(p, tmp, len); p += len;` unicode escape executes with a formatted length that is larger than the remaining checked budget, so the copy advances `p` to the post-escape cursor beyond the budget that the earlier 6-byte precheck assumed.

Immediately after the overlong unicode escape, `written = (p - (buf + *off));` records the post-copy cursor as a value larger than `available`, so later remaining-space arithmetic in the same call wraps instead of rejecting the next escape.

The trailing control-byte branch reuses the same overrun `written` value at line 650 and calls `encoded_to_buf(p, tmp, len)` on the final `\\u0000` escape, producing the AddressSanitizer heap-buffer-overflow write.

edges.relation: The post-copy cursor offset produced by the overlong unicode escape is assigned directly into `written`, preserving the out-of-budget position as the state that every later remaining-space check in this call will reuse.

The same overrun `written` value computed after the unicode escape is reused by the next control-byte guard and sink in the same `flb_utils_write_str()` call, so the wrapped remaining-space arithmetic no longer blocks the final control escape before `encoded_to_buf()` writes past the SDS allocation.
